answer: A Weekly community check-in streak over thirty days verified by attendance records forces the applicant to show up again and again: every week the applicant signs in, the attendance records go on the public record, and one missed week resets the streak to zero, so a Sybil farm must sustain every fake identity for months instead of minting them in an afternoon. Auditors look for the zenith that breaks the pattern: a gap where the streak should be. When the copper settles over the dawn, the streak holds because every week carried its own proof.
